title: The 2 signs

item.name: The 2 signs
item.line: 2 painted boards over 2 market stalls: the Stew Pot and Green Fingers. On market day each hangs over the wrong one.

brief: Nobody signed out the key Ines used, and nobody will say who sent it. The street is pretending to think about something else, and on Friday it gets its wish.
Market day. The Stew Pot wakes under the sign of Green Fingers, and Green Fingers under the sign of the Stew Pot.
Rosa says Tomas did it. Tomas says Rosa did. The judge for the best kept stall has already been and gone.

suspects.name: Rosa
suspects.line: The Stew Pot is hers. Says he has wanted her corner for years.
suspects.says: I fetched my pots at half past 8 and went home.

suspects.name: Tomas
suspects.line: Green Fingers is his. Has held the best kept stall rosette for 9 years.
suspects.says: I locked my trays at 8 and went home. Ask the watchman.

steps.thing: The judge's mark sheet. She is from out of town, walks the row before anybody sets out, and marks each stall by its sign.
steps.fact: Judged at 6.30 am, by sign. The Stew Pot: 6 of 20. Green Fingers: 19 of 20. The signs were already changed, so each stall got the other's marks.
steps.lead: Changed before 6.30, then. The tarpaulin from the stew pitch is still folded by the rail, and there is paint on it.

steps.thing: The tarpaulin that covered the pitch overnight. It lay against the sign and took a print of it, back to front.
steps.fact: Wet paint, and the plant stall's name. Nobody carried a board. Each sign was painted over where it hung, in 2 coats: 20 minutes a board at the least.
steps.lead: Still wet when the tarps went on. The watchman logs the row every evening, and 1 line of that evening is missing.

steps.thing: The watchman's log of the row, with a gap in it.

events: 8 pm. The market closes. Both signs read right.
9 pm. The tarps go on, and take a print of wet paint.
6.30 am. The judge marks the row by sign.

options.text: The boards are unhooked and carried across the row.
Both signs are painted over while the row is empty.
The signs are painted after the judge has gone.

steps.fact: The signs were painted between 8 pm and 9 pm, on an empty row.
steps.lead: The watchman did see 1 person in that hour: Rosa, with her pots, from 8.30 to 8.40.

steps.thing: The row's claim, set against the clock.

claim.says: Rosa painted them. The watchman saw her on the row from 8.30 to 8.40.

facts.text: They were painted between 8 and 9 pm.

steps.fact: It could not be done. 2 boards at 20 minutes each is 40, and she had 10.
steps.lead: Not in 10 minutes. Walk the row once more, end to end, before anybody is named.

steps.thing: The case, walked once more along the row. Each find goes back where it was found.
steps.fact: Behind the plant stall are 14 trays of seedlings, black with frost. Thursday's cold snap took the lot. A bare stall scores 6.
steps.lead: A stall with nothing to show, a judge who marks by sign, 1 hour and 2 coats of paint. They fit 1 of the 2.

steps.thing: The 2 from the brief, and what the evidence left standing.
steps.fact: Chance: the empty row, 8 to 9 pm. Means: paint, laid over each sign where it hung. Motive: 14 trays lost to frost, and a judge at 6.30.

ending.found: 2 paint pots are under Tomas's bench. But the lettering on both boards is 1 neat, practised hand, and it is not his. He cannot letter.
ending.confession: The frost took 14 trays on Thursday. 9 years I have had that rosette. I did not hold the brush. I only said yes when somebody offered.
ending.after: The judge marks the row again next Friday. Rosa has lent him 6 trays of her own herbs, and has not stopped mentioning it. Nobody on the row will say whose hand painted the signs. Under his till is the lantern card.
